issuer.summary: Maple Labs is a Cayman entity with a doxxed team, 8+ audits, a $1M bug bounty and roughly three years of clean operation on the Syrup line. This axis scores the entity, so it is identical for syrupUSDT and syrupUSDC. What a holder is trusting is discretion rather than a mechanism: redemption is a processed queue rather than an entitlement, the authority that processes it carries a threshold of one, and governance sits behind a 3-day timelock held by the same two keys that govern the sibling pool. See the full report for the loan book, queue mechanics and governance path.
issuer.summary_source: Issuer assessment and admin-topology reads, resolved live against the authority walk. This axis scores the shared entity and must move together with syrupUSDT. [verified 2026-08-22]
facts: ⚠️ THE EXIT IS DISCRETIONARY. Redemption is a PROCESSED QUEUE, not an entitlement — no holder can force their own way out, and the pool delegate can decline to process. The authority that does it carries THRESHOLD 1.

⚠️ Protocol governance runs via governor -> GovernorTimelock at 3 days, THRESHOLD 2 — and it is the SAME TWO KEYS that govern syrupUSDT, not an equivalent pair. The two Syrup products do not provide independent governance.
✅ Maple Labs (Cayman), doxxed team, 8+ audits, $1M bug bounty, and roughly a three-year clean operating record on the Syrup product line — a stronger track record than most of this corpus.

⚠️ THIS AXIS SCORES THE ENTITY, so it is IDENTICAL for syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT — Maple curates both. Per-asset differences (different pools, different collateral mixes) belong on Structural and legitimately differ there.
⚠️ The recorded defeat condition for this asset's authority model is 'governance-role-capture-2-eoas' — two externally-owned keys, which is the same count as the governance threshold.

⚠️ NOT priced here and stated to prevent double-counting: the loan book's composition, the collateral mix and the Loans/Liquidity split are Backing and Structural facts. This axis prices the OPERATOR's discretion and record.

⚠️ PROCESS NOTE, kept because it explains a past divergence: this score was published for both Syrup assets with nothing upstream holding it, so the producer feed borrowed structural_score (6.5 / 6.0) and emitted it into a field named issuer_score — overriding the authored 5.5 on two live public surfaces. the published report remains the authoring surface for both.

⚠️ syrupUSDT's loan book is MORE concentrated than syrupUSDC's — typically ~90-95% of the pool is third-party institutional credit against ~70-80% for the sibling, with a smaller pool-owned liquidity layer and fewer borrowers. That is a Backing and Structural difference, not an issuer one, and it does not move this axis.
